1.

Maneesh Yadav-Appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to challenge the order dated 24.05.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge / Special Judge (S.C./S.T. Act), Gorakhpur, whereby his application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail, during the pendency of trial in Case Crime No.
740 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(V) Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Police Station Badahalganj, District Gorakhpur has been rejected.
2.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has argued that the complainant has falsely implicated the accused-appellant in the above mentioned case and there is no such evidence collected during investigation which would even remotely suggest the alleged commission of crime by the appellant.

He further submits that as per prosecution itself, complainant's sister is 19 years old, who in her statement recorded during investigation under Section 164 Cr.P.C., did not mention about use of force by the appellant for setting up the physical relations.

He has further drawn the attention of the court to the statement of victim recorded during trial to contend that she has not supported the Maneesh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69524005/
1 prosecution case, who has been declared hostile.

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the impugned order is not based upon correction appreciation of facts and circumstances of the case, therefore, he prays that the same be set aside and the appellant be released on bail.
3. Though, on the last date of hearing, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 had appeared, but today no one has put in appearance on behalf of the complainant.

4. The prayer is opposed by learned A.G.A. who has argued that the sister of the complainant is minor who is below 18 years, and that apart, the impugned order is based upon the facts and circumstances available before the trial court, as the ground that sister of complainant turned hostile was not available before the trial court, as her evidence before the trial court was recorded after dismissal of the bail application.
He submits that since grounds set up by the appellant was not pleaded before the trial court, therefore, on this ground the appellate jurisdiction cannot be invoked by the appellant.
He prays that the appeal be dismissed.

5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering their submissions, this Court finds that the appellant is in custody since his arrest on 31.10.2023 and the statement of complainant's sister recorded during investigation under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C.
contain material variations.

The argument by the learned State counsel that the victim was minor when the alleged offence was committed is refuted by the learned counsel for the appellant, who drew attention to the statement of Principal, Lal Bahadur Shastri Inter college recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. to point out that the complainant's sister was born on 07.08.2003, therefore, was not minor.

6. The other argument by learned State Counsel that the plea regarding the main witness turning hostile had not been raised before the trial court, therefore, the same cannot be appreciated by this Court, is also misplaced, particularly when learned State Counsel is unable to controvert the stand of learned counsel for the appellant.

7. Thus, considering the above background, the custodial period undergone by the appellant as well as the fact that the material witness stands examined this court deems it appropriate to extend the regular bail to appellant.

8. Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of the case, the impugned order dated 24.05.2024 is set aside, the bail application filed by the appellant under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is hereby accepted, and it is ordered that the appellant- Maneesh Yadav be released on regular bail in the above case crime subject to his furnishing the requisite bail bonds and surety bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court.

9. The appeal is allowed.
Order Date :- 15.7.2024 Manoj  Maneesh Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69524005/
